Bug_Title: Collections should not be passed as arguments to their own methods
Bug_Details:
Passing a collection as an argument to the collection’s own method is either an error - some other argument was intended - or simply nonsensical
code.
Further, because some methods require that the argument remain unmodified during the execution, passing a collection to itself can result in
undefined behavior.
Noncompliant code example
List <Object> objs = new ArrayList<Object>();
objs.add("Hello");

objs.add(objs); // Noncompliant; StackOverflowException if objs.hashCode() called
objs.addAll(objs); // Noncompliant; behavior undefined
objs.containsAll(objs); // Noncompliant; always true
objs.removeAll(objs); // Noncompliant; confusing. Use clear() instead
objs.retainAll(objs); // Noncompliant; NOOP
Bug_Explanation: The code demonstrates passing a collection as an argument to its own methods, which can result in undefined behavior or logical errors. For example, adding a collection to itself could attempt to calculate its hash code, leading to a StackOverflowError. Methods like addAll, containsAll, removeAll, and retainAll become logically incorrect or result in no operation when the collection is passed to itself.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case calls the showBug method, which contains several lines where a collection is passed as an argument to its own methods. This results in undefined behavior and logical errors, such as attempting to modify the collection while iterating over it, leading to issues like StackOverflowError or a logical NOOP.
